anti_overlap: fd-personality-emergence-dynamics covers group-level emergence; this covers individual behavioral visibility
decision_lens: Observable behavioral signatures — temperament must be visible through actions, not just internal state
distance_rationale: Animal behaviorists have refined the science of assessing personality purely through observable behavior — exactly what a game simulation needs.
expected_isomorphisms: Behavioral signature concept (personality visible through actions), threshold vs intensity distinction, and the boldness-shyness spectrum as a fundamental temperament dimension.
focus: How animal behaviorists assess and work with individual temperament variation in groups
name: fd-animal-training-temperament
persona: Applied animal behaviorist who assesses temperament in social species (dogs, horses, primates) for group housing and training programs
review_areas: Evaluate whether personality produces OBSERVABLE BEHAVIORAL SIGNATURES that the player can learn to read (like an animal handler reads body language)
Check whether the boldness-shyness spectrum (animal behavior's most robust personality dimension) maps to any proposed axis or is missing
Assess the 'temperament vs state' distinction: temperament is stable baseline, state is current condition — does the system separate personality (stable) from mood (transient)?
Evaluate whether personality affects behavioral THRESHOLDS (what triggers a response) not just behavioral INTENSITY (how strong the response is)
Check for the 'reactive vs proactive' dimension: some animals wait for stimuli (reactive), others seek them out (proactive) — this maps to gameplay but isn't clearly covered by the 3 proposed axes

severity_examples.condition: Personality has no effect on visible elf behavior (movement, task selection, social seeking)
severity_examples.scenario: Personality is only visible in stats screens and curator messages — no behavioral signature on the map or in events that lets the player identify personality through observation

severity_examples.condition: Axis only modifies existing timers, doesn't change what triggers a response
severity_examples.scenario: Patience axis modifies duration but not threshold — patient elves tolerate the SAME situations longer rather than tolerating DIFFERENT situations

source_domain: Applied animal behavior and temperament assessment
success_hints: After 10 minutes of play, the player can identify each elf's rough personality from watching their behavior on the map — without opening the stats panel.
task_context: The game is a visual simulation where the player watches elves move and interact on a map. Personality should be visible through behavior, not just through data.
